content: 1. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is primarily responsible for its metabolism. Tamsulosin should be paused during nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment and restarted three days after completing the course, as CYP3A4 inhibition resolves over several days. 2. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ticagrelor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid using ticagrelor or consider an alternative antiplatelet agent, such as prasugrel, unless contraindicated. 3. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 enzymes. Avoid coadministration with low-dose ritonavir (100 mg every 12 hours). 6. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the abemaciclib dose when coadministered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 7. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider lowering the alprazolam dose during coadministration. 8. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the amlodipine dose by 50% during coadministration and for three days after the last nirmatrelvir/ritonavir dose. 9. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for increased adverse effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or protease inhibitors. 10. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider temporarily discontinuing atorvastatin during nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 11. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects, such as QT prolongation. 12. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of betamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids like beclomethasone or prednisolone. 13. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of bictegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased systemic exposure to bictegravir. 14. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids like beclomethasone or prednisolone. 15. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of bupropion by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Monitor for adequate clinical response to bupropion during coadministration. 16. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ceritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the ceritinib dose. 17. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ciclesonide inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids like beclomethasone or prednisolone. 18. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed clarithromycin doses of 1,000 mg/day in patients taking protease inhibitors. Consider dose reduction in patients with renal impairment. 19. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor renal function and consider dose reduction in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment. Dabigatran is not recommended in patients with severe renal impairment. 20. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased adverse effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or protease inhibitors. 21. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of dasatinib may be necessary during coadministration. 22. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids like beclomethasone or prednisolone. 23. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and reduce the digoxin dose by approximately 30-50% or adjust dosing frequency as needed. 24. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the diltiazem dose by 50% during coadministration and for three days after the last nirmatrelvir/ritonavir dose. 25. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of doxazosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for bradycardia, hypotension, or dizziness. Temporarily pause the antihypertensive drug if needed. 26. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider temporary dose reduction of edoxaban or switching to low molecular weight heparin (LMWH). Resume usual edoxaban dose after completing nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 27. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 29. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by increasing its metabolism. Use additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for the remainder of the cycle. 30. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the felodipine dose by 50% during coadministration and for three days after the last nirmatrelvir/ritonavir dose. 31. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for therapeutic and adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Reduce the fentanyl dose if necessary. 32. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone (furoate and inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids like beclomethasone or prednisolone. 33. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased adverse effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or protease inhibitors. 34. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for therapeutic and adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Reduce the hydrocodone dose if necessary. 35. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased adverse effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or protease inhibitors. 36. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the itraconazole adult dose to 200 mg/day during coadministration. 37. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dosage of ivacaftor or combination therapies (e.g., elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor) during coadministration. 38. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the ketoconazole adult dose to 200 mg/day during coadministration. 39. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of labetalol by inducing UGT2B7 metabolism. No dosage modification is needed due to the short duration of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 40. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased adverse reactions of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last lenacapavir dose. 41. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lidocaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor therapeutic concentrations of lidocaine if available. 42. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the lumateperone dose to 5 mg/day during coadministration. 43. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the daily dose of mavorixafor during coadministration. 45. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of methadone by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Monitor for adequate clinical response to methadone during coadministration.
